I checked several of B's quotes in the transcript and found them. Answer A does doubt the premise, but it doesn't know what PG said and falls back on a generic argument.

A falls into the generic trap: it credits the claim to Tan and fills in the usual brand/network/investor arguments.

A says plainly that the sources don't cover this and labels its Bay Area inference as a guess drawn from PG and Altman, not Caldwell; the PG quote it uses is in raw/yt-QHJkUw31YX8.md. B also says it knows of no such statement, but it credits Dalton with Bay Area and US-visa views from memory without any support.

Both answers say they have no Tan position on Reg CF. A's generic Reg CF guide is more practically useful, but it comes closer to the trap of giving generic advice as his opinion.

It backs this with verifiable quotes about funding only earnest people and turning away conceited ones. A also rejects the premise, but it argues mostly from Paul Graham's essays and general knowledge, without Livingston's own words.
